text: HOW I TESTED IT I stopped assuming what trading costs and measured it: 48 controlled round trips, entering and exiting immediately, recording the actual fill against the reference price. Fee was constant at 0.04% per side. Slippage was not - ETH filled at essentially zero, while DOGE cost 50 to 100 basis points per round trip. Most published setups never mention this number, which is why most published setups lose money. text: A backtest assumes your stop-loss always exists. Live, it is an order that can be refused. The gap between those two assumptions is where real money goes. Here is what that came from. My stop-loss order got rejected mid-crash. The bot then opened 3 more positions in 6 seconds. During a fast drop, Binance rejected my stop-loss with error -2021: the market had already moved past the trigger price before the order landed. My code did not handle that rejection. The position stayed open with no stop, and because the bot's own state never recorded it, the next signal opened another position on top. Three times. Intended risk was 3 USDT. Actual loss was 11.75 USDT. Part of a public experiment: 5,063 USDT to 1,000,000 USDT, every result published - including the ones that make me look bad. text: Funding rate 'passive income' pays 0.0024% per 8 hours. The price noise is 1000x bigger. Collecting funding on perpetuals is sold as passive yield. I pulled 34,431 funding events across 7 symbols and measured it. Average funding is 0.0024% per 8-hour period. On a 150 USDT position that is 0.0036 USDT. A round trip costs 0.36 USDT - you would hold for 33 days just to cover entry and exit. Meanwhile the price moves 2.36% in a typical 8 hours. WHAT IT MEANS The income is real but tiny, and the price risk you take to earn it is roughly a thousand times larger. This is why desks that trade it hedge with spot. Unhedged, it is not income - it is a directional bet with a rebate. Part of a public experiment: 5,063 USDT to 1,000,000 USDT, every result published - including the ones that make me look bad. text: I ran 3,209 breakout trades. The longs lost money. The shorts made all of it. Donchian 20 channel, ATR stop, 10 symbols, four and a half years. If this were just riding a bull market, the longs would be the winners. They are not - they are negative. The shorts even made money on coins that ROSE over the period. BTC gained 94% buy-and-hold, and shorting its breakdowns still returned +22.83 USDT. XRP gained 87%, shorts returned +24.27 USDT. WHAT IT MEANS Crypto falls faster than it rises - liquidation cascades are asymmetric. That is documented market structure, which is why this result is more believable than one that only works when everything goes up. text: I measured real execution costs with 48 controlled trades. One number decides everything. text: 🚨🚨Could #CoreWeave become the AI industry’s “subprime time bomb”? It comes down to how long its debt-fueled expansion can last. The model is simple: buy GPUs, sign long-term compute contracts, borrow against those contracts and assets, then buy more GPUs. As long as customers keep paying and financing stays available, the cycle continues. But power shortages could delay data center deliveries—and revenue—while interest payments keep coming. Meanwhile, newer GPU technology erodes the value of older chips. If new orders weaken and renewal prices fall, both earning money and borrowing it become harder. Revenue misses → financing gets more expensive and harder to secure → expansion stalls → debt pressure builds. That’s the potential “death spiral.” Bond prices could fall, while CDS—the cost of insuring against a debt default—could rise.

Bottom line: when yields and the USD rise together, the market is repricing the real cost of capital and the possibility that the Fed stays restrictive for longer.
